confidence_explanation: The analysis shows a clear pattern of unauthorized access and data exfiltration. The user (user_10) logged in from an unusual IP (45.79.97.21) and systematically accessed and downloaded sensitive files across three different departments (Executive, Sales, and Finance) over three consecutive days. This pattern of read-then-download behavior across departmental boundaries is a classic indicator of data exfiltration.

attack_chain.description: Initial unauthorized access via login from an unusual IP (45.79.97.21) instead of the baseline IP (192.168.1.110).
Commencement of data exfiltration by downloading sensitive executive configuration files.
Expansion of data collection to include sales department reports.
Expansion of data collection to include finance department files.
Persistence of unauthorized access on a second day from the same unusual IP.
Continued bulk downloading of files across Sales and Executive directories.
Large scale download of executive budget data.
Third day of unauthorized access, demonstrating a sustained pattern of data collection.
Final large-scale download of executive summary files before logout.

gaps: Lack of geolocation data for IP 45.79.97.21 to confirm if it is a known VPN or malicious proxy.
No information on whether user_10 was traveling or if their credentials were compromised via phishing.
narrative: User_10's account was used to access and download a significant volume of sensitive data across the Executive, Sales, and Finance departments over a three-day period. The activity originated from an unusual IP address and follows a premeditated pattern of reading and downloading files, indicating a successful data exfiltration incident.
